claim_summary: SAGE decomposes univariate time-series anomaly diagnosis into specialized analyzers, evidence aggregation, and analyst-facing reports, supported by dual series representations and synthetic contrastive references.

claim_evidence.quote: We propose SAGE (Specialized Analyzer Group for Expert-like Detection), a multi-agent LLM framework for structured anomaly diagnosis in univariate time series.
SAGE introduces specialized Analyzers for point, structural, seasonal, and pattern anomalies, together with an evidence-grounded Detector that aggregates heterogeneous tool evidence.

modules.name: Precise-tool and compressed-LLM temporal views
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK no: preserving precise values and constructing a compressed series representation do not themselves embed anomaly criteria; the temporal interface can remain when the task changes. R3_2_GTS yes: both representations depend on temporal-series values and numerical fidelity.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - representation interface does not embed anomaly criteria
R3_2_GTS:yes - preserves temporal data and numerical meaning
R4:Interface and Interaction; Tools and Execution

evidence.quote: SAGE therefore separates each input into two representations: the original time series for tool-based computation and a compressed summary for token-efficient LLM prompting.
This separation allows SAGE to reduce LLM input length without sacrificing the numerical fidelity required by statistical and signal-processing tools.

modules.name: Specialized anomaly analysis and evidence aggregation
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK yes: analyzer outputs, anomaly intervals, candidate types, and evidence-strength confidence directly implement anomaly diagnosis. Counterfactual: a different task family requires replacing the anomaly taxonomy, analyzer tools, and confidence-scoring objective.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - family-specific anomaly evidence and anomaly-record decisions
R4:Tools and Execution; Planning and Orchestration

evidence.quote: SAGE groups nine anomaly types into four anomaly families and assigns one specialized Analyzer to each family.
The Detector aggregates the family-specific Analyzer outputs and analyzer-generated diagnostic visualizations to produce anomaly intervals, confidence scores, and anomaly types.

modules.name: Normal-reference synthetic contrastive retrieval
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK yes: anomaly-type-specific perturbations and candidate-driven retrieval serve confidence scoring and type diagnosis. Counterfactual: changing task family requires replacing the anomaly injection taxonomy and candidate-conditioned reference selection.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - anomaly taxonomy drives contrast construction and retrieval
R4:Tools and Execution; Memory and Context

evidence.quote: SAGE constructs the ICL database from normal-reference training segments after excluding labeled anomalous intervals from the reference pool.
At inference time, SAGE retrieves the top-k = 3 most similar normal prototypes using Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) [24] with LB_Keogh pruning [12].

temporal_validity.quote: We preserve temporal order in train/test splits; the training portion is used only to extract normal patterns and construct the synthetic ICL database, not for parameter learning.

task_performance.quote: SAGE achieves the best average performance on all metrics, obtaining 0.663 Point-F1, 0.851 PA-F1, 0.910 Affiliation-F1, and 0.849 Delayed-F1 on average.

notes: Synthetic anomaly pairs serve as internal in-context references rather than an independent data augmentation task.
